blocks.value: Everything you have written so far assumed the happy path. The user types a number when you ask for a number. The array index is in range. The file exists.
Real programs do not get that. Real users type `"banana"` into a number field. Real files go missing. Real division sometimes divides by zero.
When that happens, Java does not quietly return a wrong answer. It **throws an exception**, and if nobody catches it, your program crashes. This lesson is about catching it.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Explain what an exception is and when Java throws one
Distinguish checked exceptions from unchecked (runtime) exceptions
Create and throw your own exception type
